steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Component 1 examines Key Films in US and UK cinema, testing your ability to analyse and evaluate film language, representation and context.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Section A focuses on US film, requiring detailed knowledge of your set US film including its production context, genre conventions and representations.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Section B focuses on UK film, requiring understanding of your set UK film including its social context, institutional background and cultural significance.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Both sections include extract-based questions where you analyse a sequence using precise film language terminology and connect techniques to meaning.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: For extract questions, always plan your key moments before writing to ensure a structured response rather than a shot-by-shot list. In representation questions, discuss how the representation is constructed through film language, not just whether it is positive or negative. For production context questions, always connect institutional facts to specific features of the film: do not just list context information. Practise writing under timed conditions regularly so that time pressure does not undermine your ability to structure coherent arguments. Learn specific, detailed examples for each set film that you can adapt to different question types in the exam.
